newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday March 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday March 12.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Luciano Violante and Nicola Mancino, chairmen of the lower and upper houses of Parliament, defended their institutions' operating procedures, yet said reforms are urgently needed to speed up proceeding times of bureaucracy (all).

* Following a decree law suggested by labour minister Tiziano Treu, another 700 billion lire should be assigned to create new jobs. According to the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) the funds are not sufficient. Violante said an agreement between the majority coalition government and the opposition over the emergency situation of the labour market would be now extremely useful (all).

* Civil service minister Franco Bassanini denied a report that the government was studying the possibility of freezing early retirement by civil servants for a year. Nevertheless, some 100,000 civil servants, mostly teachers, are expected to leave their jobs. Trade unions repeated that it is essential not to alter the 1995 agreement (all).

* The board of San Paolo Holding announced that it was initiating steps for the offer of shares to the public for Italy's largest commercial bank. The operation will take place in the form of a public share offer for around 25 percent while there will also be a private placement to Italian and foreign institutional investors for a further 20 percent (all).

* Italy's Italcementi Group, the largest cement producer in the European Union, is eyeing expansion opportunities in the Far East and South America to add to its strength in Europe and North America (all).
* At the Italian Treasury's auction on Tuesday the yield of short-term BOT bills fell under six percent

* Michele Tedeschi, chairman of Italian state industrial holding IRI, said the group must consider converting preference shares in state motorway manager Autostrade into ordinary ones for its privatisation. Tedeschi added that in the sell-off process 10 to 15 percent of Autostrade's capital should be reserved for a stable core of shareholders. Autostrade's results for 1996 are little changed from 1995, when it made a profit of 195.5 billion lire (Il Sole 24 Ore).
* Banco Ambrosiano Veneto reported a net consolidated profit of 190 billion lire in 1996 versus 181 billion in 1995 (all).
* Italy's Lucchini group announced it will invest 72 million ECUs in a Warsaw-based steel mill that it controls during the second phase of the factory's modernisation (Il Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
